sentences.text: 1 8. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the challenge in the present Appeal is limited to one ground i.e., contributory negligence.
It is contended that the deceased had imbibed alcohol and thus he had contributed to the accident.
9. Learned Counsel for Respondent Nos.1 to 4/claimants, who appears on advance service, refutes this contention.

Learned Counsel submits, firstly, that no evidence on this aspect was ever placed before the learned Tribunal, and secondly, that even if the deceased had imbibed alcohol, it had to be shown that the alcohol was above the permissible limit.
There is no evidence placed in this regard.

Lastly, it is contended by the learned Counsel for Respondent Nos.1 to 4/claimants that reference to the person having alcohol in paragraph 16 of the Impugned Award is to the person who was the passenger in the vehicle along with the deceased and not the deceased himself.
10. On this limited aspect, issue Notice.
Learned Counsel for Respondent Nos.1 to 4/claimants accepts Notice and submits that he has not received the copy of the paperbook.
10.1 Let a copy of the complete set of paperbook be supplied to the learned Counsel for the Respondents/claimants during the course of the day.
10.2 Since the liability, as per the paragraph 39 of the Impugned Award, is only on the Insurance Company, the service to Respondents No.5 may be This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 29/06/2025 at 21:10:43 dispensed with.
11.
Subject to the deposit of entire decretal amount inclusive of up-to-date interest within a period of 6 weeks, the operation of the Impugned Award shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.

12. Upon deposit by the Appellant, 60% of the deposited amount inclusive of up to date interest,
shall be released to the Respondent Nos.1 to 4/claimants in accordance with the scheme, as is set out in the Impugned Award.
13. The Registry is directed to place on record the digital copy of the Trial Court Record duly paginated and bookmarked in accordance with the rules of the High Court.
The parties shall act based on the digitally signed copy of the order.
TARA VITASTA GANJU, J MAY 7, 2025/ ha
